messages:
daphne: Quick sync on the quantization profile sweep I landed to prod benches :bar_chart:. High-level notes and raw numbers below — TL;DR: INT8 gives the biggest cost win for batch workloads on A100/H100, FP8 shows promise for throughput on H100 but with slightly higher quality variance. Link to dashboard: https://redwood-internal/bench/quant-sweep-2024

kevin: nice. which models / seq lengths?

daphne: ran llama-2-13b and mosaicml/mpt-30b across seq=512, 1024, 2048. Regions: us-west1 (A100), europe-west1 (H100), asia-east1 (L4). Baseline is FP16 on each GPU. Eval set: conv_eval_v2 (~12k prompts, 3 reference answers each) + 2k single-turn accuracy cases for exact-match.

raj: can you drop the p50/p95 + throughput numbers here?

daphne: sure — distilled table (p50/p95 latency in ms, throughput tokens/s, quality delta = exact-match % change vs FP16 baseline):

A100 (us-west1) — FP16 baseline: p50 48ms / p95 110ms, 18.2k toks/s
A100 INT8: p50 28ms / p95 72ms, 34.4k toks/s (+1.89x), quality delta -0.4%
A100 FP8: p50 32ms / p95 80ms, 29.0k toks/s (+1.59x), quality delta -0.6%
A100 BF16: p50 46ms / p95 106ms, 19.0k toks/s (+1.04x), quality delta -0.0%

H100 (europe-west1) — FP16 baseline: p50 30ms / p95 68ms, 24.8k toks/s
H100 INT8: p50 14ms / p95 42ms, 56.6k toks/s (+2.28x), quality delta -0.8%
H100 FP8: p50 11ms / p95 36ms, 71.6k toks/s (+2.89x), quality delta -1.1% (higher variance between seeds)
H100 BF16: p50 29ms / p95 66ms, 25.5k toks/s (+1.03x), quality delta -0.0%

L4 (asia-east1) — FP16 baseline: p50 68ms / p95 150ms, 9.4k toks/s
L4 INT8: p50 44ms / p95 120ms, 16.0k toks/s (+1.70x), quality delta -0.9%
L4 FP8: not supported / unstable on current driver (OOM on seq=2048)
L4 BF16: p50 66ms / p95 148ms, 9.6k toks/s (+1.02x), quality delta -0.0%

mpt-30b numbers were similar trend but overall 10-15% slower than llama-2-13b on same configs (kernel packing differences).

olivia: interesting that FP8 beats INT8 on H100. is that because of tensor-core speed?

daphne: yes — FP8 path uses new NVIDIA FP8 kernels we tested (fused matmul + quant simd). H100 has better FP8 hardware throughput; A100 INT8 kernels are more mature so INT8 wins there.

maria: what about kernel choices? flash attention vs cutlass vs triton?

daphne: we ran 3 kernel stacks: flash-attn (CUDA fused), cutlass/Triton (fallback), and a custom fused-quant path for INT8. Short summary: flash-attn is best for long seqs when using BF16/FP16. For INT8 we used fused-quant + cutlass matmul (because flash-attn lacks INT8 reductions in our build). FP8 used NVIDIA's fused kernels on H100. Where possible, fused-quant + KV-cache avoidance yielded the best p95 reduction.

kevin: what's the quality metric distribution? a 1% delta could be noise.

daphne: we ran 3 random seeds + calibration on a 50k-sample holdout for perplexity and exact-match. INT8 median delta = -0.4% (A100) to -0.8% (H100); 95th percentile of delta across prompts ~ -2% for worst-case prompts (numeric-heavy). FP8 median = -0.6% with larger stddev; some prompts flipped answer categories in ~0.5% of cases. We also ran top-k BLEU-ish lexical checks for generation — changes were consistent with EM deltas.

raj: does this change our recommended default profile for Dedicated vs Hosted?

daphne: recommended defaults: Hosted (latency-sensitive, mixed traffic): BF16/FP16 on H100 in europe + A100 in us-west as conservative default. Provide INT8 option for batch-heavy / throughput-tier plans. Dedicated (reserve) customers can opt-in to INT8 profiles for cost savings; we should require a short eval (5k prompts) to check quality delta tolerance. For Private on-prem, warn about driver/kernel compatibility (FP8 needs recent NVIDIA stack).

olivia: capacity sizing asks — how many replicas per 100 QPS?

daphne: rough rule-of-thumb (llama-2-13b, seq=512, avg tokens per request=150):
- H100 FP16: ~1 replica handles ~220 QPS (p95 goal 200ms)
- H100 INT8: ~1 replica handles ~480 QPS (p95 ~120ms)
- A100 FP16: ~1 replica handles ~160 QPS
- A100 INT8: ~1 replica handles ~300 QPS
- L4 FP16: ~1 replica handles ~90 QPS
These are conservative with autoscale headroom. Include token-aware autoscaling in the console.

bench-bot: Uploaded raw CSVs to /gcs/bench/quant-sweep/1718254321/ (files: a100.csv, h100.csv, l4.csv)

kevin: any regressions to watch for in production?

daphne: yes — numeric/numeric reasoning, code outputs, and long-context factual consistency. Ops: add per-route quality monitors (we already have eval hooks) and regression alert if exact-match drops >1.5% or perplexity increases >3% on a rolling 24h sample. Also include rollback action to FP16 automatically.

maria: can you paste the exact command used so eng-releases can re-run?

daphne: command we used (example):
```
python tools/bench/quant_runner.py \
  --model llama-2-13b \
  --quant int8 \
  --gpu a100 \
  --region us-west1 \
  --batch 8 \
  --seq 2048 \
  --eval-set conv_eval_v2 \
  --tokens 200000 \
  --kernels fused_quant,cutlass \
  --save /gcs/bench/quant-sweep/1718254321/a100.csv
```

olivia: great. let's add a short playbook entry for sales/infra: cost delta estimates per 1M tokens?

daphne: rough cost delta (based on current instance rent): INT8 on A100 -> ~45% token-cost reduction vs FP16. FP8 on H100 -> ~55% reduction but with more QA required. I'll draft a 1-pager.

kevin: thanks — can you also add a short note about fallback rules? if INT8 p95 > 2x baseline fallback to fp16?

daphne: added to playbook: if p95 latency or EM quality breach, automatic fallback to pinned FP16 model variant for that route. I'll open a follow-up thread for the playbook draft.

maria: ack, will coordinate with solutions for customer opt-ins.

olivia: thanks all :tada:
